title: A brief perturbation. A broad transcriptional signature: psilocin human-neuron transcriptomics
description:
Explore the results in the interactive transcriptomic atlas.

This record is an independent secondary analysis and derived research object. It is not the original Schmidt experimental dataset or the original Hoffrichter/Schmidt analysis.

Original experiment and data generation: Schmidt et al. generated the human iPSC-derived cortical-neuron data and reported the experiment in Psilocin fosters neuroplasticity in iPSC-derived human cortical neurons (2026), doi:10.7554/eLife.104006. The associated source research data are deposited at Dryad, doi:10.5061/dryad.xsj3tx9w3, under Dryad's CC0 framework.

Original analysis: the Hoffrichter/Schmidt RNA-seq analysis code is pinned at Git commit c565709affafbea09406bd7b42fe494f08db6cce and preserved by Software Heritage as swh:1:dir:c847a8a51074c59d651e3258cf1355936e921048.

This secondary analysis: Christopher B. Germann independently reanalysed the public RNA-seq data. This archive contains the newly generated reproducibility code, frozen specifications, derived tables, figures, tests, and a static copy of the interactive atlas. Schmidt et al. are cited as the source-study authors; they are not creators of this research object.

Version 1.0.1: documentation and interpretation clarifications; analytical results are unchanged from version 1.0.0.

The analysis identifies a broad OXPHOS-centered transcriptional signature at both sampled days. It reports the complete primary pathway family, gene-level estimates, leading edges, prespecified robustness checks, and bounded exploratory analyses. Because control harvest days are unresolved, a treatment-specific temporal trajectory is not estimable. Transcriptional enrichment does not establish respiration, ATP production, redox flux, DNA-repair activity, or telomere preservation.
